items.title: Section: Six Frameworks for Internal, External, and Internal-External Observation

items.zh: 復有差別。謂若緣自內定地輕安俱行色為境，是名於內身住循身觀。若緣自內不定地麁重俱行色為境，是名於外身住循身觀。若緣他輕安俱行、麁重俱行色為境，是名於內外身住循身觀。如是若緣依前三色所生受、心、法為境，隨其所應，當知即是住循三觀。復有差別。謂若緣內能造大種色為境，是名於內身住循身觀。若緣外能造大種色為境，是名於外身住循身觀。若緣依能造大種色所生根境所攝造色為境，是名於內外身住循身觀。如是若緣依前三色所生受、心、法為境，隨其所應，當知即是住循三觀。復有差別。謂若緣有識身內色為境，是名於內身住循身觀。若緣無識身有情數青瘀等位色為境，是名於外身住循身觀。若緣無識身色於過去時有識性，有識身色於未來時無識性，相似法性、平等法性為境，是名於內外身住循身觀。如是若緣依前三色所生受、心、法為境，隨其所應，當知即是住循三觀。復有差別。謂若緣自中身髮毛、爪、齒等相為境，是名於內身住循身觀。若緣他中身髮、毛、爪、齒等相為境，是名於外身住循身觀。若緣內表身變異、不變異青瘀等相，及緣外表身變異、不變異青瘀等相、相似法性、平等法性為境，是名於內外身住循身觀。
items.en: There is, further, this distinction: taking as object the form bound up with pliancy in one's own concentrated state is dwelling in observation of the internal body; taking as object the form bound up with grossness in one's own unconcentrated state is dwelling in observation of the external body — and their combination, in oneself and others, is the internal-external body. Further: taking the causal great elements themselves as object is the internal body; what they produce, in the sense-faculties and their objects together, is the external and internal-external body. Further: taking the living, conscious body as object is the internal body; taking the lifeless, discolored corpse as object is the external body; and seeing the shared, equal nature running through both — one presently conscious, bound eventually for the same unconsciousness — is the internal-external body. Further: taking one's own hair, body hair, nails, and teeth as object is the internal body; another's, the external body; and seeing the shared, equal nature of both the living surface and its eventual visible decay, whether one's own or another's, is the internal-external body.

items.zh: 如是若緣依前三色所生受、心、法為境，隨其所應，當知即是住循三觀。如是等類身、受、心、法諸差別門當知多種，今於此中，且顯少分諸門差別。

items.title: Section: Why Four Foundations — Countering the Four Inverted Views

items.zh: 又為對治四顛倒故，世尊建立四種念住。謂為對治於不淨中計淨顛倒，立身念住。以佛世尊於循身念住中，宣說不淨相應四憺怕路。若能於此多分思惟，便於不淨斷淨顛倒。為欲對治於諸苦中計樂顛倒，立受念住。以於諸受住循受觀，如實了知諸所有受皆悉是苦，便於諸苦斷樂顛倒。為欲對治於無常中計常顛倒，立心念住。以能了知有貪心等種種差別，經歷彼彼日夜、剎那、瞬息、須臾非一眾多種種品類心生滅性，便於無常斷常顛倒。為欲對治於無我中計我顛倒，立法念住。由彼先來有有我見等諸煩惱故，無無我見等諸善法故，於諸蘊中生起我見。以於諸法住循法觀，如實了知所計諸蘊自相、共相，便於無我、斷我顛倒。
items.en: Further, the Bhagavān established the four foundations of mindfulness specifically to counter the four inverted views. To counter the inverted view that takes the impure for pure, body-mindfulness is established. To counter the inverted view that takes suffering for pleasant, feeling-mindfulness is established. To counter the inverted view that takes the impermanent for permanent, mind-mindfulness is established. To counter the inverted view that takes the selfless for possessing a self, phenomena-mindfulness is established — by dwelling in observation of phenomena, truly knowing the particular and universal characteristics of the very aggregates one has mistakenly clung to, one thereby cuts off the inverted view of self within what has no self.

items.title: A Second Rationale: Countering Delusion at Its Root

items.zh: 復有差別。謂諸世間，多於諸蘊唯有蘊性、唯有法性不如實知，橫計有我依止於身；由依身故，受用苦樂；受苦樂者，由法非法，有染有淨。為欲除遣我所依事愚故，立身念住。
items.en: There is, further, this distinction: worldly beings, for the most part, do not truly know that the aggregates are simply aggregates, that phenomena are simply phenomena — and so they falsely posit a self dependent on the body. Dependent on that body, they experience pleasure and pain; and as one who experiences pleasure and pain, through righteous or unrighteous action, they become defiled or purified accordingly. In order to dispel the delusion regarding what this self is falsely taken to depend on, body-mindfulness is established.

items.zh: 為欲除遣我所領受事愚故，立受念住。為欲除遣於心、意、識執我愚者我事愚故，立心念住。為欲除遣所執我心能染淨事愚故，立法念住。

items.title: Two Further Rationales: Through Karma, and Through Defilement and Purity

items.zh: 復有差別。謂若依此造作諸業，若為此故造作諸業，若造業者，若由此故造作諸業。為總顯示如是一切，立四念住。當知此中，依止於身造作諸業，為求受故造作諸業，心能造業，由善不善法能造諸業。復有差別。謂若依此有染有淨，若為此故起染起淨，若染淨者，若由此故成染成淨。總為顯示如是一切，立四念住。
items.en: There is, further, this distinction: that in dependence on which karmic action is performed; that for the sake of which karmic action is performed; that which performs karmic action; and that by which karmic action is performed — to fully display all of this, the four foundations of mindfulness are established. There is, further, this distinction: that in dependence on which defilement and purity occur; that for the sake of which defilement and purity arise; that which is defiled or purified; and that by which defilement and purity come about — to fully display all of this, the four foundations of mindfulness are established.

items.zh: 當知此中，依止於身有染有淨，為求受故起染起淨，心染淨者，由諸法故成染成淨。

items.title: Section: What "Establishment of Mindfulness" Means — Fascicle 28 Complete

items.zh: 問：念住何義？答：若於此住念、若由此住念，皆名念住。於此住念者，謂所緣念住。由此住念者，謂若慧、若念攝持於定，是自性念住；所餘相應諸心心法，是相雜念住。又由身、受、心、法增上所生善有漏、無漏道，皆名念住。
items.en: Question: What is the meaning of "establishment of mindfulness"? Answer: both that in which mindfulness abides, and that by which mindfulness abides, are called establishment of mindfulness. That by which mindfulness abides is: wisdom and mindfulness themselves, held together in concentration, are establishment of mindfulness in its intrinsic nature; the remaining associated mental factors are establishment of mindfulness in its mixed nature. Further, whatever wholesome mundane or supramundane path arises through the power of body, feeling, mind, or phenomena is likewise called establishment of mindfulness.

items.title: Section: Hearing, Reflection, and Cultivation — Fascicle 28 Complete

items.zh: 此復三種。一、聞所成，二、思所成，三、修所成。聞思所成，唯是有漏；修所成者，通漏無漏。
items.en: This is, further, of three kinds: that accomplished by hearing, that accomplished by reflection, and that accomplished by cultivation. … What is accomplished by hearing and by reflection is solely tainted; what is accomplished by cultivation spans both tainted and untainted.

blocks.text: Why there are exactly four foundations of mindfulness. Fascicle 28 ends today.

Six frameworks for internal and external: for example, "taking as object the form bound up with pliancy in one's own concentrated state is observing the internal body", the body outside concentration, external. Master Cháng Bǎi: in absorption there is pliancy; outside it, the body is heavy.

"The Bhagavān established the four foundations to counter the four inverted views": body-mindfulness against taking the impure as pure; feeling-mindfulness against taking suffering as pleasure; mind-mindfulness against taking the impermanent as permanent; phenomena-mindfulness against "taking the selfless as possessing a self".

"Worldly beings do not truly know that the aggregates are simply aggregates", so they imagine a self depending on the body, experiencing feeling, being the mind, and acting through phenomena. Each foundation dispels one of these.
Another rationale: the body is what karma depends on; feeling, what it is done for; mind, what does it; phenomena, the karma itself. Master Cháng Bǎi: one acts to gain pleasant feeling or avoid pain.

"Both that in which mindfulness abides, and that by which it abides, are called establishment of mindfulness": the objects, and "wisdom and mindfulness themselves, held together in concentration". It is accomplished by hearing, reflection, and cultivation; "what is accomplished by hearing and reflection is solely tainted; what is accomplished by cultivation spans both".
Training, its supports and failures, yoga, attention, and the four foundations of mindfulness. Fascicle 29 continues with the remaining factors of awakening.

quiz.q: One framework: form with pliancy in one's concentrated state is internal, form with grossness in the unconcentrated state external. What do the masters say?
options: Cháng Bǎi: in absorption there is pliancy; out of it the body is heavy and unworkable; Miào Jìng: once pliancy fades after absorption, that is insight practised outside absorption
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: in absorption there is pliancy; out of absorption is the unconcentrated level, where the body is heavy and the elements lack workability. Venerable Miào Jìng: some time after leaving absorption the pliancy is gone — that is insight practised outside concentration. The English reads "internal-external" as self and others combined; the original speaks only of others.

quiz.q: What order of practice does Venerable Miào Jìng give for internal and external body observation?
options: beginners can only take their own body; one must observe oneself first, then others
quiz.why: "Taking the living, conscious body as object is the internal body." Venerable Miào Jìng: one just beginning the foundations of mindfulness cannot take another's living body as object, only one's own.

quiz.q: Phenomena-mindfulness counters taking the selfless as self. What does Venerable Miào Jìng say ordinary people mostly take as self, on close inspection?
options: mostly the mind, consciousness — not form, feeling, perception, formations
quiz.why: "To counter the inverted view that takes the selfless for possessing a self, phenomena-mindfulness is established." Venerable Miào Jìng: looked at closely, most cling to the mind — consciousness — as self, not to form, feeling, perception, or formations.

quiz.q: In the second rationale, why is body mindfulness established, and what does Master Cháng Bǎi say about the body?
options: to dispel delusion about what the self depends on; the body isn't healthy just because one wishes — it needs conditions
quiz.why: "In order to dispel the delusion regarding what this self is falsely taken to depend on, body-mindfulness is established." Master Cháng Bǎi: it isn't that the body is healthy because you want it to be, or ill because you choose — it takes many conditions.

quiz.q: The third rationale speaks of karma: in dependence on, for the sake of, who acts, and by what. How do the masters map "for the sake of"?
options: Cháng Bǎi: one acts to seek pleasant or avoid painful feeling — this shows feeling-mindfulness; Miào Jìng: it is for the sake of feeling, seeking pleasant experience
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: one creates karma to pursue pleasant feeling or avoid painful feeling — this shows feeling-mindfulness. Venerable Miào Jìng: in a word, it is for feeling — seeking pleasant experience, one does all sorts of things.

quiz.q: The fourth rationale speaks of defilement and purity. How does Venerable Miào Jìng say it differs from the third, on karma?
options: the karma before is that of birth and death; defilement and purity here include undefiled karma
quiz.why: "That in dependence on which defilement and purity occur; that for the sake of which they arise; that which is defiled or purified; and that by which they come about." Venerable Miào Jìng: the karma earlier should be karma of birth and death; defilement and purity here should include undefiled karma.

quiz.q: What is accomplished by hearing and reflection is solely tainted; cultivation spans both. How do the masters explain?
options: Cháng Bǎi: reflective wisdom only suppresses afflictions; tainted cultivation only suppresses; untainted cultivation uproots the seeds; Miào Jìng: up through highest worldly dharma is tainted, after the path of seeing untainted
quiz.why: "What is accomplished by hearing and by reflection is solely tainted; what is accomplished by cultivation spans both tainted and untainted." Master Cháng Bǎi: tainted cultivation can only suppress afflictions; only untainted cultivation uproots the seeds of greed and hatred. Venerable Miào Jìng: "tainted" is at the stages of warmth through highest worldly dharma; after the path of seeing it is untainted.
